review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

1:1.sourceText: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ κατ’ ἐπιταγὴν Θεοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τῆς ἐλπίδος ἡμῶν
1:1.targetText: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to a command of God our Savior, and of the Lord Jesus Christ our hope,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness title addition: LSV the Lord follows TR κυρίου with Jesus Christ; pinned N1904 writes Christ Jesus without a Lord token.

review.note: The two Christ/Jesus title pairs are reversed in English order relative to pinned N1904. Each actual name/title is linked by identity, not by target position.

1:2.sourceText: Τιμοθέῳ γνησίῳ τέκνῳ ἐν πίστει· χάρις, ἔλεος, εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν.
1:2.targetText: to Timotheus—genuine child in faith: Grace, kindness, peace, from God our Father and Christ Jesus our Lord!

groups.note: The mercy/compassion noun ἔλεος is rendered kindness by LSV here; it retains the actual mercy head rather than borrowing a different ordinary kindness noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness possessive addition: LSV our Father follows additional TR ἡμῶν; pinned N1904 has God Father without our at that occurrence.

1:3.sourceText: Καθὼς παρεκάλεσά σε προσμεῖναι ἐν Ἐφέσῳ, πορευόμενος εἰς Μακεδονίαν, ἵνα παραγγείλῃς τισὶν μὴ ἑτεροδιδασκαλεῖν
1:3.targetText: According as I exhorted you to remain in Ephesus—I going on to Macedonia—that you might charge certain [ones] not to teach any other thing,

groups.note: The compound ἑτεροδιδασκαλεῖν means teach differently/other doctrine; LSV expands that one verb as to teach any other thing, without inventing separate any/other/thing Greek tokens.

1:4.sourceText: μηδὲ προσέχειν μύθοις καὶ γενεαλογίαις ἀπεράντοις, αἵτινες ἐκζητήσεις παρέχουσιν μᾶλλον ἢ οἰκονομίαν Θεοῦ τὴν ἐν πίστει·
1:4.targetText: nor to give heed to fables and endless genealogies, that cause questions rather than [the] stewardship of God which [is] in faith.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English definite article is supplied with anarthrous Greek stewardship; the later Greek article introduces which in the faith modifier.
English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

review.note: LSV stewardship agrees with N1904 οἰκονομίαν; the pinned TR instead has οἰκοδομίαν, edification. The source article introducing the faith modifier supplies which only, not a being verb.

1:5.sourceText: τὸ δὲ τέλος τῆς παραγγελίας ἐστὶν ἀγάπη ἐκ καθαρᾶς καρδίας καὶ συνειδήσεως ἀγαθῆς καὶ πίστεως ἀνυποκρίτου,
1:5.targetText: And the end of the charge is love out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of unhypocritical faith,

1:6.sourceText: ὧν τινες ἀστοχήσαντες ἐξετράπησαν εἰς ματαιολογίαν,
1:6.targetText: from which certain [men], having swerved, turned aside to vain discourse,

1:7.sourceText: θέλοντες εἶναι νομοδιδάσκαλοι, μὴ νοοῦντες μήτε ἃ λέγουσιν μήτε περὶ τίνων διαβεβαιοῦνται.
1:7.targetText: willing to be teachers of law, not understanding either the things they say, nor concerning what they confidently assert,

groups.note: The first μήτε is coordinated under the explicit preceding not understanding; English therefore uses either ... nor without repeating a second not at either.

1:8.sourceText: Οἴδαμεν δὲ ὅτι καλὸς ὁ νόμος, ἐάν τις αὐτῷ νομίμως χρῆται,
1:8.targetText: and we have known that the Law [is] good, if anyone may use it lawfully;

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

1:9.sourceText: εἰδὼς τοῦτο, ὅτι δικαίῳ νόμος οὐ κεῖται, ἀνόμοις δὲ καὶ ἀνυποτάκτοις, ἀσεβέσι καὶ ἁμαρτωλοῖς, ἀνοσίοις καὶ βεβήλοις, πατρολῴαις καὶ μητρολῴαις, ἀνδροφόνοις,
1:9.targetText: having known this, that law is not set for a righteous man, but for lawless and insubordinate persons, ungodly and sinners, impious and profane, murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, manslayers,

1:10.sourceText: πόρνοις, ἀρσενοκοίταις, ἀνδραποδισταῖς, ψεύσταις, ἐπιόρκοις, καὶ εἴ τι ἕτερον τῇ ὑγιαινούσῃ διδασκαλίᾳ ἀντίκειται,
1:10.targetText: whoremongers, homosexuals, enslavers, liars, perjured persons, and if there be any other thing that is adverse to sound doctrine,

groups.note: This maps the installed LSV wording homosexuals to its actual compound noun ἀρσενοκοίταις. The correspondence records this translation choice; it does not supply a separate modern identity noun in Greek.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English there be supplies an existential introduction after Greek if any other thing; no independent Greek being/existence verb is printed there.
English adds a relative that before is adverse; the Greek finite adverse predicate directly describes the conditional any-other-thing subject.

1:11.sourceText: κατὰ τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς δόξης τοῦ μακαρίου Θεοῦ, ὃ ἐπιστεύθην ἐγώ.
1:11.targetText: according to the good news of the glory of the blessed God, with which I was entrusted.

groups.note: The accusative relative refers to the entrusted good news; LSV renders the passive entrusting complement as with which, without a separately written Greek with preposition.

1:12.sourceText: Χάριν ἔχω τῷ ἐνδυναμώσαντί με Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ Κυρίῳ ἡμῶν, ὅτι πιστόν με ἡγήσατο θέμενος εἰς διακονίαν,
1:12.targetText: And I give thanks to Him who enabled me—Christ Jesus our Lord—that He reckoned me steadfast, having put [me] to the ministry,

groups.note: The χάριν ἔχω idiom literally has thanks and means I am thankful/I give thanks; its noun and finite verb jointly support this English thanksgiving expression.

The one actual με object of He reckoned me faithful is also the understood object of the accompanying having put into ministry participle. English repeats that same first-person object as bracketed me, preserving its actual identity without an extra Greek pronoun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV opening And follows TR καί; pinned N1904 begins directly with the thanksgiving idiom.

1:13.sourceText: τὸ πρότερον ὄντα βλάσφημον καὶ διώκτην καὶ ὑβριστήν· ἀλλὰ ἠλεήθην, ὅτι ἀγνοῶν ἐποίησα ἐν ἀπιστίᾳ,
1:13.targetText: who before was speaking slander, and persecuting, and insulting, but I found kindness, because, being ignorant, I did [it] in unbelief,

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English object it is supplied for did; pinned N1904 has no separate object pronoun there.

review.note: Greek describes the former person as blasphemous, a persecutor, and insolent; LSV recasts those nominal/adjectival characterizations as speaking slander, persecuting and insulting. These are the same actual character/action heads, not extra Greek speaking verbs. The passive mercy verb ἠλεήθην means I was shown mercy, rendered I found kindness.

1:16.sourceText: ἀλλὰ διὰ τοῦτο ἠλεήθην, ἵνα ἐν ἐμοὶ πρώτῳ ἐνδείξηται Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τὴν ἅπασαν μακροθυμίαν, πρὸς ὑποτύπωσιν τῶν μελλόντων πιστεύειν ἐπ’ αὐτῷ εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
1:16.targetText: but because of this I found kindness, that Jesus Christ might first show forth all long-suffering in me, for a pattern of those about to believe on Him to continuous life.

groups.note: The actual passive mercy verb means I was shown mercy; LSV recasts the beneficiary experience as I found kindness without inventing an independent find verb.

The Greek dative πρῴτῳ qualifies me, in me as first/foremost (echoing first among sinners in1:15). LSV places first before show forth, an English adverbial attachment; the actual ranking word remains linked with that scope difference explicit.
The prospective participle μελλόντων with believe is rendered about to believe; about expresses that impending predicate, not a separate Greek around preposition.
